clue.text: Cleared the backlog when fully involved

definitions.meaning: to have dealt with all the work that had piled up
engrossed or entangled in something, as one is in a story or a scandal

explanation.surface: Someone finally clears their backlog after throwing themselves into the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having brought one's work level after falling behind and being thoroughly absorbed or entangled in something.

clue.text: Grip a college lantern

parts.note: a lantern is a kind of lamp

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a lantern belonging to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamp is to hold tightly, as a vice holds.

clue.text: Ask for aid, but find no takers

definitions.meaning: to go round asking for charity
said of something on offer that nobody wants

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help but nobody responds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to beg, and also of a thing to remain unclaimed because nobody wants it.

clue.text: Naming a book "the songster"

definitions.meaning: a songster is a singing bird; an old name for a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone gives a book the name 'The Songster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a heading to a work is one sense; the other is a dialect name for the pipit or similar small songbird.

clue.text: Appeal with positive justification for parks, maybe

parts.note: a plea is an appeal
being positive is being sure
grounds are reasons or justification

explanation.surface: Someone appeals, with confident reasoning, for more parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Parks are an example of open land laid out for recreation, so 'maybe' marks them as one instance.

clue.text: Reinforce the fact that meat is costlier

definitions.meaning: read literally: the price of a cow's flesh has gone higher

explanation.surface: Someone shores up the claim that the butcher's prices have risen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means strengthen; read word by word it also says the price of steak has risen.

clue.text: Withdraw with lumbago?

definitions.meaning: to pull out of an arrangement
lumbago is lower back pain, read whimsically as one's spine having gone out

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws, citing a bad back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means retreat from a commitment; read literally it suggests a back that has 'gone out' with pain.

clue.text: Trader from Florida organising riots

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

indicators.note: organising puts things into order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A merchant from Florida is stirring up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist sells flowers, so is a kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Claimed to have been given advance treatment

definitions.text: to have been given advance treatment

explanation.surface: Someone said they had been treated ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means professed falsely; split after its first three letters it reads as looked after early.

clue.text: Practically everyone brought a plant container back

parts.note: everyone is all of them

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the container is turned round

parts.note: a tub is a large pot for growing plants

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody returned a flowerpot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nearly or almost, as in being nearly finished.

clue.text: Alec rose prepared a vegetable

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Alec Rose cooked a vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' signals an anagram of ALEC ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive of the broad-leaved kind is a salad vegetable, so it is an example.

clue.text: Error over housing joyless travellers

indicators.note: housing means the first piece holds the second within it
over in an across clue means the word for a mistake is turned backwards

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
grim means bleak and cheerless

explanation.surface: A mistake is made in lodging some unhappy travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the mistake word in an across answer, and 'housing' wraps that reversal round the bleak word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilgrims are people who journey to a holy place, so they are a kind of traveller.

clue.text: About to receive short message by e-mail

parts.note: on means concerning, as in a talk on art
dropping someone a line means sending a brief note

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get a brief message sent electronically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to receive' reads as 'soon to get'; 'About' is really a word meaning concerning, and 'to receive' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Communicating over the internet, as e-mail does, is being connected to the network.

clue.text: Name girl disposed to feign illness

indicators.note: letters disposed are set out in a new order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A named girl seems inclined to fake being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'inclined' with 'to'; it is the anagram signal for NAME GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be ill to dodge work or duty.

clue.text: Play many a role with mad abandon

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: doing something with abandon is unrestrained, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor overacts many a part with wild abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandon' rearranges A ROLE and MAD into ELODRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage drama, so it is a kind of theatre piece.

clue.text: Tried to send educational journal to Edward

parts.note: TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' paper
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to post a teaching magazine to a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES is a British weekly for schoolteachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tried and tested both mean put to the trial or examined.

clue.text: The latest from cork journalists

parts.note: a cork is a stopper, so it stops a bottle
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: News arrives from reporters in the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cork' looks like the Irish city; it is a bottle stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Late news added to a paper after printing has begun gives the most recent reports.

clue.text: Was slow to get the piping clad

definitions.meaning: wrapping pipes in insulating material to keep heat in

explanation.surface: Someone was slow to have the pipes insulated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trailed behind, and also covered pipes with insulating jacket, so both senses fit.

clue.text: German youngsters displaying brilliance

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: German children show great talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is sparkling light, so it is a form of brightness or showy splendour.

clue.text: He must ensure there's filling for the cavity

definitions.text: He must ensure there's filling for the cavity

parts.words: He must ensure there's filling for the cavity
parts.note: it sounds like a builder or baker, but the cavity is a hole in a tooth and the filling is amalgam

explanation.surface: Someone has to be sure there is enough to fill a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional treats teeth, packing decay holes with amalgam.

clue.text: Avoid having to complete the course

definitions.meaning: to circumvent a problem or rule
to go all the way around a golf course or race circuit

explanation.surface: Someone dodges having to finish the round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means circumvent a difficulty, and also finish a lap or round of a course.

clue.text: Restrict single pressman in London

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for the capital

parts.note: town is a traditional name for London, as in going up to town
I is the Roman numeral one
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: Someone restricts a lone journalist working in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to limit someone's freedom, constraining them.

clue.text: Welshman and Scotsman? The devil it is!

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
mon is a Scots form of man, used in address

explanation.surface: A Welshman and a Scotsman turn up, and the speaker exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The devil it is!' sounds like an oath; the definition is 'The devil'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek belief a daimon was a spirit, the source of the later word demon.

clue.text: Frank has a scheme for extended living space

parts.note: frank means candid, open
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A man called Frank has a design for a bigger lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a layout has few interior walls, so rooms flow into one large living area.

clue.text: The pits in Ghana direly need investment

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the words Ghana direly

explanation.surface: Mines in Ghana are badly in need of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' looks like mines; it means the lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of fortune, and 'the pits' is slang for the worst there is.

clue.text: Its arena is constructed well

indicators.note: something constructed is assembled from parts, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A stadium is built properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like an adverb ('built well'); it is the noun, a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is one where water rises under its own pressure, so the adjective names that type of bore.

clue.text: Started to write in a dictionary

indicators.note: in means the word for writing goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone began writing entries in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened means began, as in a meeting started or opened.

clue.text: A Frenchman's right to be ingenious

parts.note: droit is the French word for right

explanation.surface: A Frenchman claims his right to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, close in sense to resourceful.

clue.text: Malevolent and wrong with outlandish rites

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so these letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Something evil and wicked is going on with strange rituals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening harm, suggesting evil intent.
